## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the display order of the seven areas a stated requirement, or only implied by the enumeration order used in US3 and FR-019? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §FR-019]
  - PASS: `data-model.md` §5 models `order` as an explicit field ("1..7 contiguo, en el orden de FR-017"), turning the enumeration order in FR-017 into a normative, testable value rather than an implication.

- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define what the Inicio view presents under SPEC 002 (retain, restyle, or replace the SPEC 001 area list), given FR-031–FR-034 change the surrounding structure? [Gap, Spec §FR-031, §FR-033, §FR-034]
  - PASS (resolved in current spec): FR-059 (added in the 2026-09-08 clarification session) explicitly answers this — retain SPEC 001's purpose (identity + brief explanation + 7-area overview with availability status), restyled with the definitive visual identity and consistent `ModuleHeader`, anchored by SC-030.

- [x] CHK003 Are the icon→concept mappings in FR-019 stated as normative requirements or as illustrative examples? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
  - PASS: FR-019 uses "DEBE"; `data-model.md` §5 labels its icon-concept table "concepto, no implementación" — clarifying these are normative at the concept level (the icon must evoke that idea) without mandating an exact visual/implementation. Not merely illustrative.

- [x] CHK004 Is the "explicación breve de incorporación futura" for the six unavailable views specified as a single consistent text or as per-module text? [Completeness, Spec §FR-044]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.6 and `tasks.md` T014 both resolve this as a single shared content constant (`idaf.unavailableBody`), reused identically across the six views.

- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for navigation behavior at the minimum supported width — may it wrap, scroll, or condense — beyond "permanecen visibles y utilizables"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-046]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): FR-046 stays generic. `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §4 gives partial design-level guidance ("la nav puede estrecharse pero no desaparece") without fully specifying wrap vs. scroll vs. condense. SC-021 only requires visibility+usability at 1024px, not a specific layout mechanism, so this is acceptable but not fully specified.

- [x] CHK006 Does the spec state that each nav entry always renders its text label (independent of icon state), as the completeness basis for FR-024? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, §FR-024]
  - PASS: FR-018 states unconditionally "El nombre DEBE permanecer visible junto al icono" — independent of icon state — which is exactly the completeness basis FR-024's fallback relies on.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 For FR-021, is it defined whether color may count as one of the "dos señales visuales simultáneas", or must both signals be non-color? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021]
  - PASS: FR-021 explicitly resolves this — at least one of the ≥2 signals must be non-chromatic, but color may be an additional (not the only) signal; color alone is explicitly declared insufficient.

- [x] CHK008 Is "un cambio leve de color" quantified so that a compliant vs. non-compliant active-state color treatment can be distinguished? [Measurability, Spec §FR-021]
  - PASS: quantifying "leve" is unnecessary given the superseding rule — any color-only change, however strong, fails the "≥1 non-chromatic signal" test, so the compliance line is drawn by signal type, not color magnitude. Anchored by SC-031.

- [x] CHK009 Is "un único lenguaje visual (una misma familia)" defined by checkable attributes (grid, stroke, style), or assessed only via the SC-013 association result? [Measurability, Spec §FR-020, §SC-013]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §2 I1 gives concrete, structurally checkable attributes (one 24×24 viewBox, `fill="none"`, constant `stroke-width`/`stroke-linecap`/`stroke-linejoin`, one `paths.ts`), verified in `registry.test.ts` — not assessed only through the subjective SC-013 panel result.

- [ ] CHK010 Is "icono visualmente distinguible" clarified — distinguishable from the other nav icons, legible at navigation size, or both? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): SC-013's association rubric (≥0.90 mean, ≥0.60 floor) covers inter-icon distinguishability, but no explicit criterion addresses legibility at the actual navigation render size (e.g., a minimum icon dimension). The shared 24×24 grid convention (`contracts/visual-system.md` §2 I1) is a reasonable design-level answer, but there is no spec-level legibility-at-size criterion.

- [x] CHK011 Is "alternar rápidamente entre módulos" quantified (switch rate, number of switches) for FR-023 and SC-011? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023, §SC-011]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK022 — research D8 and `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` R11 pin ≥20 rapid switches, echoed by SC-031 and exercised at ~25 in `quickstart.md` E6.3.

- [x] CHK012 Are the conditions under which "un icono no puede mostrarse" defined, so the fallback requirement is testable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024, §CL-07]
  - PASS (with note): because icons are inline SVG (research D7 — "con SVG en línea no hay petición de red que falle"), a real icon-render failure is structurally near-impossible by design; the condition is deliberately simulated via forced CSS-hiding (`quickstart.md` E6.6, `nav-icons-active.spec.ts`) rather than a naturally occurring trigger. The fallback itself remains fully testable via that simulation.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Is "en cada momento DEBE haber exactamente un módulo principal marcado como activo" (FR-022) consistent with states where no protected module applies (login screen) and with transient states during navigation and reload? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-009]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/auth-session.md` CHK017 — the public `/login` zone never mounts `PrimaryNav` at all, and the `loading` transient renders no nav either (`contracts/auth-and-session.md` §E1), so FR-022 only ever applies where `PrimaryNav` is actually mounted — no conflicting state exists.

- [x] CHK014 Do FR-018 ("el icono complementa al texto y NUNCA lo reemplaza") and FR-024 ("el nombre textual … permite seguir identificándolo") agree that the text label is always present? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-024]
  - PASS: both requirements rely on and restate the same guarantee — the text label is always rendered, independent of icon state.

- [x] CHK015 Are the "≥ 2 señales" of FR-021 and the "exactamente uno activo / cero excepciones" of SC-010 and SC-011 mutually consistent and jointly sufficient to define the active state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §SC-010, §SC-011]
  - PASS: the three requirements are complementary, not overlapping — FR-021 defines the visual encoding, SC-011 the cardinality invariant, SC-010 the usability outcome — and SC-031 explicitly unifies all three anchors into one criterion.

- [x] CHK016 Is FR-017's "exactamente las siete áreas … NO DEBEN crearse nuevas áreas" consistent with FR-048's allowance to modify the existing visual/navigation structure? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, §FR-048]
  - PASS: the two requirements operate on different axes — FR-017 fixes the area **count**, FR-048 permits restyling the **visual/structural treatment** of the existing areas — with no overlap or contradiction.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Is the reload-in-a-module scenario (FR-009 / CL-03) specified so the correct nav entry is active immediately on restore, not merely eventually? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009, §FR-022, §CL-03]
  - PASS: `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §3 N5 derives the active state from the current route rather than a separately-synced flag, and §E4 confirms rehydration completes before the first protected render — so the correct entry is active at first paint, not eventually.

- [x] CHK018 Are the requirements for navigating to an unavailable module (allowed; shows "No disponible") versus an unknown route (redirect) kept distinct so the two behaviors are not conflated? [Coverage, Spec §FR-026, §FR-043, §FR-053]
  - PASS: FR-026/FR-043 (one of the 7 known areas, possibly unavailable) and FR-053 (a route matching none of the 7 areas) are mutually exclusive route categories with clearly distinct, non-conflated behaviors, per `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §1's route table.

- [x] CHK019 Does FR-044's "sin … botones que aparenten operar" state whether the unavailable views contain any interactive elements at all? [Clarity, Spec §FR-044]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.6 goes further than the spec's wording with a categorical prohibition (no `button`/`input`/`form`/`select`/`role="button"`/action links/data tables at all), fully resolving the ambiguity at the design level.

- [x] CHK020 Beyond FR-025's prohibition of duplicate entries, is there a requirement covering how a future module is added to navigation without creating two entries for one capability? [Coverage, Spec §FR-025, §FR-017]
  - PASS: FR-025/SC-038's single-source `MODULE_REGISTRY` pattern structurally prevents duplicate entries for any future addition too (Principio V, plan.md Constitution Check); adding a **new** area is itself explicitly out of scope for this spec (FR-017), so no additional spec-level requirement is needed beyond the architectural guarantee already in place.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK021 Does SC-010 ("módulo activo … en 3 segundos o menos … 100 % de los intentos sobre las siete áreas") define the evaluation setup (evaluators, trials per area)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010]
  - PASS: spec §Evaluación con personas gives the panel (≥5), the literal per-area prompt (P6), and the timing table (t0/t1/instrument/threshold) for SC-010.

- [x] CHK022 Is SC-012 ("con el icono oculto, el 100 % sigue siendo utilizable por su nombre") backed by a defined way to force the icon-hidden condition? [Measurability, Spec §SC-012, §FR-024]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK006 — `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` N2 and `quickstart.md` E6.6 define the exact forcing method (`svg{display:none}` via DevTools).

- [x] CHK023 Is SC-014 ("cero elementos simulados") accompanied by a definition of what counts as a simulated element (chart, metric, device, operative button) so the check is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §SC-014, §FR-044]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK005 — `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.6 enumerates the prohibited set explicitly.
